tier_reason: The ePrint 2025/1867 paper (published in TCHES 2026, DOI 10.46586/tches.v2026.i1.302-324) benchmarks sign_core against the C-FN-DSA reference at commit 96e3b92 (Table 6) and states the compiler (GCC 13.3.0, Clang 10.0.0, GCC 13.2.0), the flags (-O2, -DFNDSA_SHAKE256X4=1, per-ISA -m/-march flags) and the CPUs (i7-11700K, Cortex-A72, SpacemiT X60). The artifact repo ships the benchmark code for both sides (opt/speed_fndsa.c and ref/speed_fndsa.c with per-platform Makefiles, plus profiling/ for BaseSampler and FFT) and the raw outputs (opt/ and ref/speed_fndsa_*.txt), which match Table 6.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Falcon-512 sign_core cycles vs the C-FN-DSA reference: 1.13x SSE2, 1.23x AVX2, 1.36x AVX-512F, 1.17x NEON, 1.37x RV64GC, 1.36x RV64GCB, 1.58x RV64GCV, 1.59x RV64GCVB (the paper reports these as 13-59% improvements). Falcon-1024: 1.14x-1.59x. The BaseSampler core without PRNG is 4.2x (SSE2), 8.4x (AVX2), 9.8x (AVX-512F), 7.7x (RVV), 3.8x (RV64IM) and 1.8x (NEON) faster than the C-FN-DSA ref core. With PRNG included it is 1.3x-2.7x. RVV FFT/iFFT is 4.1x-4.7x faster than ref on the SpacemiT X60, and RV64D FFT/iFFT is 2.7x-3.0x faster.
corrections.baseline: C-FN-DSA (Thomas Pornin's FN-DSA/Falcon implementation, github.com/pornin/c-fn-dsa at commit 96e3b92), SHAKE256X4 variant
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 13.3.0 (x86-64, Ubuntu 24.04); Clang 10.0.0 (ARM, Ubuntu 20.04); GCC 13.2.0 (RISC-V, Bianbu 1.0.15). All builds use -O2 -DFNDSA_SHAKE256X4=1. x86 builds pin the ISA with -msse2, -mavx2 or -mavx512f plus -mno-* flags for higher extensions. RISC-V builds use -march=rv64gc, rv64gc_zba_zbb, rv64gcv or rv64gcv_zba_zbb.
corrections.workload: Falcon-512/1024 sign_core (SHAKE256X4 PRNG variant; SHAKE256X8 on AVX-512F) CPU-cycle medians over 10,000 runs (x86, ARM) or 2,000 runs (RISC-V) across SSE2, AVX2, AVX-512F, NEON, RV64GC, RV64GCB, RV64GCV and RV64GCVB. Also micro-benchmarks of the vectorized BaseSampler and the RVV/RV64D FFT/iFFT.
corrections.license: MIT (root LICENSE). The C-FN-DSA-derived opt/ and ref/ directories carry the Unlicense. opt/fft_neon.c is Apache-2.0 (derived from GMUCERG Falcon_NEON).
corrections.caveats: Gains are for signature generation (sign_core) only, not keygen or verify, and are measured on the SHAKE256X4 variant, which is not KAT-compatible with default Falcon signing (interoperable for verification). Part of the gain comes from integrated third-party code: XKCP 8-way Keccak on AVX-512F; the BK22 hybrid Keccak and NG23 NEON FFT on ARM; ZYHK25 Keccak on RISC-V. The paper measured C-FN-DSA as faster than the NIST-submission AVX2 code on the i7-11700K, so it is a strong baseline. The only direct comparison with other optimized prior work is at the BaseSampler level (NG23 NEON is slower than ref). Licensing is mixed: MIT, Unlicense (public-domain dedication, no patent grant) and Apache-2.0 files. GitHub's detector reports NOASSERTION.

notes: All claimed numbers check out against Tables 4-6 of the paper and the repo's raw speed files. The one overstatement was 'up to 8.4x faster than prior work': 8.4x is the AVX2 BaseSampler core vs the C-FN-DSA ref, and the maximum is 9.8x on AVX-512F. The record's metric is 'throughput', but the paper measures per-signature cycle latency. Metadata verified: 4 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2025-12-05 (active), usability copyable (all components are under OSI licenses).
